symptom: `alter snippet … set (Action: show page P(Sale = $Sale)) on btn` (and `replace btn with {…}`) stored the target page with an empty ParameterMappings; check and exec passed, describe printed `(Sale = $currentObject)`, and mx check failed CE1571. The same button written by create snippet was correct.
cause: The ALTER builders never walk the stored document, so their pageArgContext is unknown (known=false), and binds() then accepts every argument as the inferred context object. The explicit by-name mapping for a document parameter was only looked up when binds() was false, so under ALTER it never was.
fix: Ask namedParameterArgument when the context is unknown as well: a page or snippet parameter is bound by name whatever encloses the widget. $currentObject and other arguments keep the old behaviour.
insight: A permissive 'unknown context' default is safe for a refusal guard but not for a decision that chooses what to write: the same flag that stops ALTER refusing also switched off the one argument form that needs no context. Test the alter path with a zero-valued argCtx, not only the create path's atDocumentRoot.
test: mdl/executor/cmd_pages_showpage_alter_snippet_2621_test.go (zero argCtx, snippet and page; control: $currentObject stays inferred); failed before the fix. Live 11.12.6: set, set inside a data view and replace all store SnippetParameter Sale, re-run unchanged, mx check 0 errors (was CE1571).
